drhp.business: KSCL manufactures sugar, alcohol and power from sugarcane at its units at Kattur and Sathamangalam in Tamil Nadu. The Company operates in three major segments — Sugar, Cogeneration of power (Cogen) and Distillery — with cane sourced from farmers in its command area, supplemented by molasses bought from other factories within and outside Tamil Nadu for the distillery. Power is sold to the state utility under a long-term PPA from the Sathamangalam unit and to open access consumers and IEX from the Kattur unit, while alcohol/ethanol is supplied to Oil Marketing Companies.

risks.note: Cane availability for the 2025-26 crushing season was lower by around 10% versus 2024-25, forcing the Company to operate the Kattur unit alone and keep Sathamangalam idle. Management states that high labour cost, better revenue from competitive crops and fear of pest & disease will adversely affect raw material availability and in turn overall capacity utilisation, with a cascading effect during the 2026-27 crushing season.
risks.risk: Sugarcane availability in the command area — structural raw-material shortage

risks.note: Pest and disease in the central part of Tamil Nadu and in the Company's own command area forced farmers to switch to alternative crops as a rotation measure, while paddy, tapioca, banana and gingelly fetch better revenue than sugarcane — directly shrinking the cane base the mills depend on.
risks.risk: Pest and disease incidence in sugarcane, and farmer switching to competitive crops

risks.note: Whenever there is surplus sugar production in the country the selling price falls below the cost of production, and because global production is usually surplus at the same time, exports also become unviable, leaving no relief valve for domestic surplus.
risks.risk: Industry oversupply — sugar selling price falling below cost of production

risks.note: Sugarcane procurement price has increased year on year (FRP up 4.50%) while the Minimum Selling Price of sugar, fixed at Rs. 31/Kg in February 2019, has not been increased, and the actual selling price is market driven — compressing the sugar segment as lower volumes raise cost of production per ton.
risks.risk: Regulated cost-price squeeze — FRP rises while MSP is frozen

risks.note: India has an estimated ethanol surplus of nearly 20 billion litres against only around 11 billion litres contracted by oil marketing companies after 20% blending was achieved in March 2025; the gap has led to underuse of distillery capacity and concerns about financial pressure across the sector, threatening the distillery leg that has been the offset to sugar.

With own molasses inadequate the Company had to procure 58,842 metric tons from other factories in and outside Tamil Nadu at higher prices, and had to absorb GST on bought-out molasses and other input credits as costs following implementation of VAT on Extra Neutral Alcohol — a structural margin leak tied to cane shortfall.
risks.risk: Molasses feedstock dependence and tax leakage in the distillery

risks.note: Vagaries in the monsoon pattern affect availability of sugarcane, the major raw material; predictions of a below-normal southwest monsoon in India during 2026 are expected to impact cane planting acreage from current levels, and reduced sales in 2025-26 were partly attributed to scanty rainfall.

Reduction in the availability of agricultural labour and a sharp increase in labour cost have a serious impact on cane cultivation, with most factories unable to get adequate cane supply to their rated crushing capacity; harvesting is the most labour-intensive and expensive activity, making mechanisation urgent.
risks.risk: Agricultural labour scarcity and rising labour cost in Tamil Nadu
